raw_policy_excerpt:
# Shopify's Bug Bounty Program

We reward security researchers for finding and reporting vulnerabilities that help keep our platform secure. Our bug bounty program offers rewards up to $200,000 and bonuses for outstanding contributions.

## Typical Bounty Amounts
Bounty amounts will be determined using Shopify's Bug Bounty Calculator. In most cases, we will only triage and reward vulnerabilities with a score greater than 0. A score under 3 will result in a $500 bounty. Scores greater than or equal to 3 will be determined by the calculator. Bonuses are determined as a percentage (10% of what the bounty is estimated at for an exploitable issue), with a minimum of $500 and a maximum of $5,000.

While our bounty table states the minimum bounty per severity, scores for non-core properties listed in scope will be determined with Environment Score modifiers set to Low for Confidentiality, Integrity, and Availability Requirements.

## Leaked Credentials
Shopify accepts reports of leaked credentials, including Authentication material for Shopify APIs and/or Shopify infrastructure. Hackers should submit the leaked credentials to the program and should not test their validity beyond authenticating and then immediately deauthenticating - without exercising any functionality.

## Rules for participation
- Only test against stores you created using your HackerOne YOURHANDLE@wearehackerone.com registered email.
- Do not attempt to gain access to, or interact with stores you didn't create.
- Do not contact Shopify Support as part of your testing or to ask about the bounty program.
- You must report any discovered vulnerability to Shopify as soon as you have validated the vulnerability.
- Your testing and submission must not violate any law, or disrupt or compromise any data that is not your own.

## Ineligible Issues (Partial)
- XSS Storefront: staff inserting JS in storefront area
- XSS iFrames, Rich Text Editor, Checkout, Set Header, Inspect Element/Console
- Self-XSS without reasonable attack scenario (max 2 steps)
- CSRF access to modify cart; CSRF Login/Logout (unless chained)
- DDoS attacks; Open Redirect without user interaction; HTML Injection in emails (unless chained)
- SSRF with HTTP/DNS interaction alone
- GraphQL introspection exposure; Password complexity; CVV validation
- cdn.shopify.com arbitrary file upload (intended functionality)
- Stored XSS on cdn.shopify.com or static.shopify.com

## Third-Party Apps
Vulnerabilities found in Shopify third party apps should be reported to the responsible developer. Only report to Shopify if no satisfactory response from developer. Shopify will not pay a bounty for vulnerabilities in third party apps.
